etymologies.etymologyHTML: From French fibre, from Old French fibre, from Latin fibra.

definitions.definition: (countable) A single elongated piece of a given material, roughly round in cross-section, often twisted with other fibers to form thread.
(uncountable) A material in the form of fibers.
(textiles) A material whose length is at least 1000 times its width.
(mathematics) The preimage of a given point in the range of a map.
(category theory) The pullback of a morphism along a global element (called the fiber of the morphism over the global element).
(computing) A kind of lightweight thread of execution.

quote.citation: 2008, Joe Duffy, Concurrent Programming on Windows, Pearson Education, →ISBN, unnumbered page:
quote.text: We've seen how to create a new fiber and convert the current thread into a fiber (which continues to run after the conversion), but we have yet to focus on how to schedule a new fiber onto the current thread.

definitions.definition: (cytology) A long tubular cell found in bodily tissue.
